properties.description:

Coastal waters from Port Fourchon Louisiana to Lower Atchafalaya
River LA from 20 to 60 NM...
Coastal waters from Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana from 20 to 60 NM...

At 1202 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a cluster of strong
thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and
small hail. This cluster of thunderstorms is generally located 23 nm
southeast of Louisiana Offshore Oil Port, or 26 nm southwest of
Southwest Pass Of the Mississippi River, moving west at 15 knots.

waves, small hail and dangerous lightning strikes. Boaters should
seek safe harbor immediately until this activity passes.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 8:28AM CDT until September 7 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River Near Alto affecting Houston, Angelina, Anderson and
Cherokee Counties.

For the Neches River...including Alto...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River near Alto.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Boat ramps and picnic areas near the river
will begin to flood. Ranchers should move cattle and equipment near
the river to higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Friday
morning to a crest of 16.4 feet early Saturday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when
walking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering
flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

For more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website
address into your favorite web browser URL bar:
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 830 AM CDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 8:09AM CDT until September 3 at 5:15PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Hardin County in southeastern Texas...
Northwestern Jefferson County in southeastern Texas...
South Central Tyler County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 807 AM CDT, Gauge reports and emergency management are
reporting flooding continuing. Flooding is already occurring in
the warned area.
- Flood water are moving down Village Creek,Little Pine Island
Bayou and Pine Island Bayou.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lumberton, Silsbee, Kountze, Sour Lake, Saratoga, Wildwood,
Thicket, Bevil Oaks, Honey Island, Village Mills, Batson and
Votaw.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
properties.area: Hardin, TX; Jefferson, TX; Tyler, TX

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 6:37AM EDT until September 4 at 8:27AM EDT by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following creek in
Pennsylvania...

Bald Eagle Creek near Beech Creek Station affecting Clinton and
Centre Counties.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following creek in
Pennsylvania...

Penns Creek near Penns Creek affecting Union and Snyder Counties.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Bald Eagle Creek near Beech Creek Station.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Homes in the cottage area are cutoff by
high water and directly affect homes in this area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 15.1 feet.
- Forecast...The creek is expected to rise to a crest of 15.3 feet
this morning. It will then fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet. Major flooding is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.6
feet on 01/19/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
